gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Flat, stencil-cut and graceful. Noto Sans Avestan, a plain sans with a tall x-height and curves that stop short of closing, keeps a full page of text easy to move through.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Sophisticated from the first glance, Bevellier draws curves and straights at a single width, cut flat like a stencil. Noto Sans Balinese brings short ascenders and breathing room inside each rounded glyph, which gives this sans-serif pairing its quiet strength.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Bevellier's stout diagonals, as heavy as its uprights, give it a stencil-cut look. Noto Sans Bamum, a sans-serif with curves that stop before turning inward, does the quieter job of keeping small text open.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Stencil-flat letters with close sidebearings and no thick-thin pulse lead the way here, in Bevellier. Noto Sans Bassa Vah, a sans-serif, brings a dominant midsection.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-batak: Bevellier looks like it was written with one fixed nib, flat and graceful, with a wide-looking lowercase and tight spacing. And Noto Sans Batak, a sans-serif with a towering x-height and an open e, takes over the reading work.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Noto Sans Bengali, a sans-serif with capitals barely taller than lowercase, reads with distinctly open letter mouths. Bevellier adds hairline-free display strokes.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Tight-coiled rope against a flat stencil cut. Bevellier's unswelling curves would feel thin if made small, but Noto Sans Bhaiksuki, a sans with open apertures, holds up at text sizes.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Graceful and sophisticated, Bevellier cuts even its g in one unchanging line weight, flat as a stencil. But Noto Sans Brahmi, a sans with a high mean line and open-ended curves, loosens the page below it.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Noto Sans Buginese reads like a chalk arc left unjoined, with short ascenders. Bevellier handles display work with marker-tip strokes and a wide-looking lowercase, while the sans below it does the quieter reading.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Noto Sans Buhid sets generous space between curve ends and stems, with a high-set x-height guiding the line. Over many lines it reads like a plain sans that never tires.
